Article Title: 'We don't have an MS Dhoni': Ex-England captain's blunt warning to Stephen Fleming
Article Text:
MS Dhoni and Stephen Fleming (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former England captain Michael Vaughan believes newly-appointed Test coach Stephen Fleming should have taken charge immediately instead of delaying his arrival until England's tour of South Africa later this year.Fleming was named England's new Test coach after Brendon McCullum was removed from the role earlier this month, though the New Zealander has retained his position as the team's white-ball coach. However, Fleming will not oversee England during the upcoming three-Test home series against Pakistan, which begins on August 19 at Headingley.Questioning the decision, Vaughan said England would miss an opportunity to help Fleming settle into the role before bigger assignments such as the Ashes."Stephen Fleming is a good appointment as England's Test coach, but he should be in position for the start of the Pakistan series, rather than taking over fully for the South Africa tour in December," Vaughan wrote in the Telegraph."It is about the small details, gaining experience of going to grounds such as Edgbaston – which hosts an Ashes Test – getting to know people involved in English cricket and fact-finding about our game by meeting the county coaches who can help him.These are the one-per-cent details England let slip during the Brendon McCullum years but are required to win major trophies."Vaughan also suggested that England agreeing to Fleming's preferred timeline reflected a shift in the appeal of the coaching role."It also suggests the England job has lost a little of its allure because he does not feel he must start immediately. It also shows a little bit of desperation that England were willing to appoint a candidate on his terms, rather than their own," he added.Fleming arrives in England after an extraordinary stint with Chennai Super Kings in the IPL. During his 17-year association with the franchise, he guided the team to five IPL titles and two Champions League trophies alongside captain MS Dhonibefore stepping down earlier this month.Vaughan, however, warned that the former New Zealand skipper would be walking into a very different environment, pointing out that England captain Joe Root does not offer the same dynamic that Dhoni did at Chennai.“Fleming is very well respected, renowned for being a very good manager and tactician. I’ve seen him at the IPL, and one of the problems he might discover in English cricket is that we do not have an MS Dhoni to be his captain.“Dhoni ran the ship at Chennai Super Kings, and Fleming had some really good backroom coaches as well. Eric Simons was a wonderful bowling coach for him, a master at getting the white ball to swing. His team was built around skill with the ball, not express pace. I wonder whether that is an indication that the skill side of bowling will come back into the England Test team rather than just out-and-out speed," Vaughan wrote.
Article Summary: Former England captain Michael Vaughan believes Stephen Fleming should have taken charge immediately. Fleming was named England's new Test coach after Brendon McCullum was removed from the role earlier this month. Fleming will not oversee England during the upcoming three-Test home series against Pakistan, which begins on August 19.

Article Title: 'I am sad, I couldn't be selected': 17-year-old aspiring woman cricketer dies by suicide
Article Text:
Representational photo (Image credit: Agencies)

Suicide note recovered

NEW DELHI: A 17-year-old aspiring woman cricketer allegedly died by suicide in Nagpur after reportedly being upset over not getting selected for a higher-level team.The incident came to light on Thursday morning in Laxmi Nagar under the Bajaj Nagar police station area.The deceased, Aditi Chaukhande, was originally from Akola and lived in Nagpur with her mother and elder brother. Her father works as a civil contractor in Akola.Aditi had recently passed her Class 12 examinations.According to police, Aditi was training as a cricketer along with her elder brother, Prabal, who is also an upcoming player.On Wednesday night, after having dinner with her mother, Aditi went to her room and allegedly died by suicide. Her brother was out of town at the time of the incident.Police said a suicide note was recovered from the room.In the note, Aditi reportedly spoke about her disappointment over not being selected and expressed her wish that her parents would be made proud.“Dada, you play so well. You will become very big. Make our parents proud. I am sad I couldn’t be selected,” the note read, according to police.Senior Inspector Chetan Chauhan said the initial investigation suggests the teenager was upset over not being selected for a higher-level cricket team.“The victim seems to have taken the drastic step due to disappointment over not getting selected in a big team,” said senior inspector Chetan Chauhan.Police have registered an accidental death case and are investigating the matter further.
Article Summary: Aditi Chaukhande was originally from Akola and lived in Nagpur with her mother and elder brother. Aditi was training as a cricketer along with her elder brother, Prabal, who is also an upcoming player. Police have registered an accidental death case and are investigating the matter.

India added two more medals to its tally on Day 8 of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, with weightlifter Lovepreet Singh winning silver and discus thrower Seema Kaliramna securing bronze to take the country's overall haul to 17 medals.The latest additions leave India 10th in the overall medal standings after Thursday's competition, with a total of 3 gold, 10 silver and 4 bronze medals.While the country did not add to its gold-medal count, another productive day in weightlifting and athletics strengthened India's position heading into the closing stages of the Games, with several more medal opportunities still to come.India's first medal of the day came in the men's +110kg weightlifting competition, where Lovepreet Singh produced the performance of his career to claim the silver medal.Lovepreet lifted 176kg in the snatch, setting a new Indian national record, before adding 212kg in the clean and jerk, another national record, to finish with a combined total of 388kg.The Indian weightlifter missed out on the gold medal by the narrowest of margins, finishing just 1kg behind New Zealand's David Liti, who claimed the Commonwealth title.The silver medal was India's eighth weightlifting medal of the Glasgow Games, underlining another successful campaign for one of the country's strongest disciplines.India's second medal arrived later in the day as Seema Kaliramna secured bronze in the women's discus throw final at the EDF Scotstoun Stadium.It was far from a straightforward competition for the Indian thrower.Seema opened the final with a foul before responding with a throw of 57.32 metres in the second round.She then produced what proved to be the medal-winning effort on her third attempt, throwing 58.65 metres to move into the bronze-medal position.The remainder of her competition was challenging, with four of her six attempts ending in fouls. However, her third-round mark proved enough to keep her on the podium.Jamaica's Samantha Hall won gold with a throw of 61.66m, while Canada's Julia Tunks took silver with 60.67m.The bronze was India's 17th medal overall and the fourth medal won by the athletics contingent at the Games.There was also heartbreak for fellow Indian thrower Nidhi Rani, who narrowly missed out on joining Seema on the podium.Nidhi steadily improved throughout the competition and reached 57.10m with her third throw but ultimately finished fourth, just outside the medals.After eight days of competition, India has collected 17 medals, comprising:The medal haul has been shared primarily between weightlifting and athletics.Athletics and para-athletics have contributed eight medals (2 gold, 4 silver and 2 bronze), while weightlifting has also produced eight medals (1 gold, 6 silver and 1 bronze). India's remaining medal has come in para-powerlifting.The latest results place India 10th in the Commonwealth Games medal standings heading into the final stretch of competition.Although India added two medals on Thursday, several other athletes fell just short of podium finishes.In the women's +86kg weightlifting competition, Martina Devi Maibam finished fifth with a combined lift of 245kg.In the men's shot put final, Tajinderpal Singh Toor also finished fifth, while compatriot Samardeep Singh Gill placed seventh.India also has a major medal opportunity unfolding in the decathlon, where Tejaswin Shankar has delivered a sensational opening day performance.He enters Day 2 in second place with 4,339 points, sitting just 14 points behind Olympic champion Damian Warner (4,353 points) after an incredible first day in Glasgow.Because the decathlon is a gruelling two-day event, his competition is only halfway done. He must now face the final five events on Day 2 to determine the final medal placements, with everything still to play for in one of the most demanding contests in athletics.Thursday also proved productive in setting up medal chances for the remaining days of the Games.India enjoyed a clean sweep in the men's javelin qualification, with Neeraj Chopra, Rohit Yadav and Yash Vir Singh all advancing to the final.Neeraj led the Indian trio with a throw of 79.61m, followed by Rohit Yadav's 78.37m and Yash Vir Singh's 78.36m, with all three comfortably progressing.There was further success in the men's triple jump qualifiers as Praveen Chithravel and Selva Prabhu Thirumaran both booked places in the final.With multiple Indian contenders still in medal contention across athletics and other disciplines, and Tejaswin Shankar poised for a dramatic decathlon finish, India will look to build on its tally of 17 medals and climb further up the standings during the closing days of the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.
Article Summary: India added two more medals to its tally on Day 8 of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Weightlifter Lovepreet Singh won silver and discus thrower Seema Kaliramna secured bronze to take the country's overall haul to 17 medals. The latest additions leave India 10th in the overall medal standings with a total of 3 gold, 10 silver and 4 bronze medals.

Article Title: Spiker-turned-goalkeeper Mohith eyes FIH World Cup splash
Article Text:
Goalkeeper HS Mohith (Image credit: Instagram)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: What began as an unwilling stint between the posts has turned into a calling. Young goalkeeper HS Mohith is now determined to impress at the upcoming FIH World Cup. If not under the bar, Mohith would have well been spiking or blocking the ball on a volleyball court.A shortage of goalkeepers at sports hostel in Hassan prompted the coach to ‘borrow’ Mohith from the volleyball team. Incidentally, the team did well in that tournament, and with his height being a disadvantage, Mohith was asked to continue with hockey.It took him barely two years to fall in love with the sport. Accepting his position, however, took longer. “I thought goalkeeping was a tough job. I went up to the coach and said I don’t want to be a goalkeeper, I want to be in forward line and score goals. It didn’t take him long to remind me that I was picked for the position and it would take them a while to train another goalkeeper,” Mohith told TOI during the World Cup preparatory camp at SAI Centre here.Disappointed but not defeated, the 24-yearold soon began looking at the role differently. “I realised how important a goalkeeper is. Unlike outfield players, who can sometimes get away with mistakes, a goalkeeper has nowhere to hide.I thrive under pressure and I started enjoying that responsibility,” he recalled.Mohith’s rise has been steady. A key member of India’s title-winning side at the 2023 Junior Asia Cup, he announced himself at last year’s Sultan Azlan Shah Cup before producing a composed display against Australia in the FIH Pro League, where he won the shootout for India.
Article Summary: Goalkeeper HS Mohith is now determined to impress at the upcoming FIH World Cup. A shortage of goalkeepers at sports hostel in Hassan prompted the coach to 'borrow' Mohith from the volleyball team. It took him barely two years to fall in love with the sport.

Article Title: Boxers pack a medal punch: Six Indians reach semifinals, assure record 10 medals
Article Text:
Sakshi Chaudhary

India’s medal tally is set to swell. After the weightlifters did their bit, on Wednesday it was the boxers’ turn to take centre stage at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.So far, 10 Indian boxers have reached their respective semifinals, assuring themselves of at least a bronze medal each. Lovlina Borgohain had made the last four of the women’s 75kg category after receiving a bye in the draw, while Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg) and Jadumani Singh (55kg) won their quarterfinal bouts on Tuesday.Boxing awards two bronze medals in each category, meaning every semifinalist is guaranteed a place on the podium.Wednesday, however, brought a six-medal windfall, beginning with Sakshi Chaudhary, who faced European Championships silver medallist Caitlin Fryers of Northern Ireland in the women’s 51kg quarterfinal. Fryers charged forward from the opening bell but Sakshi refused to be overpowered. She used her footwork well, landing clean punches before moving out of range to seal a 5-0 unanimous-decision victory.In the next bout, it was Arundhati Choudhary’s turn to shine in the women’s 70kg category. The first woman boxer from Rajasthan to compete at the CWG ensured she would not leave Glasgow empty-handed, although the contest was tougher than she may have anticipated.Her opponent, New Zealand’s Morgan Henderson, used to play rugby, and that aggression was evident in the ring. Henderson was docked a point but Arundhati matched her intensity and made the cleaner punches count to claim a 3-1 split-decision victory.In the men’s 60kg quarterfinal, world No. 5 and former World Youth champion Sachin Siwach registered a dominant 5-0 win over Botswana’s Treasure Moremi. In the men’s 80kg quarterfinal, Ankush Yadav advanced with a 5-0 unanimous-decision victory over Seychelles’ Jade Micock, while Narender Berwal completed the sweep by edging Samoa’s Michael Seko 3-2 in the men’s 90kg-plus quarterfinal.Later in the evening, Jaismine advanced to the women’s 57kg semifinals with 4-1 a win over Elise Glynn of England.India enjoyed a good day in the field too, with Tajinderpal Singh Toor and Samardeep Singh Gill progressing to the men’s shot put final. National record-holder Toor opened with 19.93m in Group A before improving to 20.14m to breach the automatic qualification mark of 20m. The twotime Asian Games champion then opted against taking his third throw.Gill qualified with his best throw of 19.95m in his first attempt in Group B. He followed it with 19.75m before fouling his third and final attempt.There was, however, disappointment in the women’s high jump final, where Asian U20 champion and national record-holder Pooja Singh finished eighth. She cleared 1.77m on her second attempt but failed to clear 1.82m. Weightlifter Sanjana Panchal was also eliminated early after failing all three snatch attempts at her opening weight of 94kg in the women’s 77kg event.
Article Summary: 10 Indian boxers have reached their respective semifinals, assuring themselves of at least a bronze medal each. Sakshi Chaudhary beat Caitlin Fryers of Northern Ireland in the women’s 51kg quarterfinal. Arundhati Choudhary won 3-1 split-decision over Morgan Henderson of New Zealand. Sudharsan set to resume batting next week

NEW DELHI: As India enter a critical phase in their bid to stay alive in the World Test Championship (WTC) race, Jasprit Bumrah and Shubman Gill are taking a cautious approach to regaining full fitness ahead of the two-Test series in Sri Lanka starting Aug 15.TOI understands that Bumrah will begin gradually increasing his bowling workload after suffering an impact injury during the ODI series in England, while Gill has sought help from specialists outside the BCCI for his chronic neck problem.It is learnt that Bumrah developed swelling in his knee before the final ODI at Lord’s on June 19 but the medical team is confident he will be ready for the first Test in Galle. The selectors picked him for the Sri Lanka tour subject to fitness. The focus is now on preparing him to endure the rigours of Test cricket.Bumrah has played little longer-format cricket since the second Test against South Africa in Guwahati last Nov. He has featured only in T20 cricket, apart from two ODIs in England last month. Bumrah is currently at the Centre of Excellence (CoE).“Bumrah will start bowling this week and his workload will be gradually increased. He needs to get used to bowling longer spells again.The medical team at CoE will be closely monitoring it, and the initial reports are that he should be good to start the first Test. These two Test matches are very important for India. Dropping even one Test here will put immense pressure on the team to qualify for the WTC final next year. That’s why the team management wants Bumrah to be available in prime shape for the series,” a BCCI source told TOI.As for Gill, it is learnt that he has been consulting specialists to address the neck pain that first flared up during his first innings in the opening Test against South Africa at Eden Gardens. The problem eventually ruled him out of the rest of the series, which India lost 0-2. He also missed an IPL match because of the recurring pain.“Gill has been battling the neck pain for some time. It flares up every now and then, especially when he bats for a longer period. He has been consulting specialists outside BCCI for treatment and he is much better now. It’s an ongoing process. India felt his absence in that South Africa series.That’s why he has taken a cautious approach in addressing the chronic issue,” the source said.Sai Sudharsan, India’s No. 3 batter in Tests, has also been selected subject to fitness. He is recovering from a hamstring injury and will resume batting at the CoE next week. The BCCI medical team has shared a positive report regarding his availability for the first Test.
Article Summary: Jasprit Bumrah will begin gradually increasing his bowling workload. Shubman Gill has sought help from specialists outside the BCCI for his chronic neck problem. India's No. 3 batter Sai Sudharsan will resume batting at the CoE next week.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Indian boxers unfazed by baggage snag on arrival
Article Text:
Santiago Nieva (Image credit: X)

India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two-week multinational training camp in Belfast, but its final preparations were briefly disrupted when some boxers’ luggage failed to arrive ahead of Thursday’s opening ceremony.The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp, during which the boxers benefitted from quality sparring and competition-specific training. However, several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.Sources said officials from the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the chef-de-mission’s office were at the airport on Wednesday, coordinating with the airline to ensure the baggage reached the contingent before the ceremony. The boxing competition begins on Friday and runs until Aug 1.The incident, however, has not gone down well with the Boxing Federation of India (BFI). Sources said that after the issue surfaced, the federation asked the boxers to submit declarations stating that they would not speak to the media about internal team matters and would instead remain focused on their performances.Despite the logistical hiccup, the mood in the camp remains upbeat. “We are settling in well in Glasgow. We had a good camp in Belfast where everybody got quality sparring and proper preparations. The boxers are managing their weights well. We will have the draws soon. We are coming with high expectations for this competition,” India women’s head coach Santiago Nieva told TOI .India’s 14-member squad features Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain and Jaismine Lamboria, the world No. 1 in the women’s 57kg category.
Article Summary: India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two- week multinational training camp in Belfast. The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp. NEW DELHI: For Gulveer Singh, spending months away from home, missing the birth of his daughter and banking solely on video calls to his family were sacrifices that found a sweet reward as the 28-year-old clinched Commonwealth Games silver.“It has been six to eight months since I got home. It’s a lonely world out there for me. I can only see the face of my child during video calls. But to represent the nation is equally important,” Gulveer had said prior to his departure.The road to Glasgow wasn’t smooth. Ankle and knee sprains disrupted preparations while the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) asked him to return from his overseas base to compete at the InterState championships and prove his fitness. On his return, although he fell short of the upcoming Asian Games qualifying mark, Gulveer and coach Scott Simmons persisted with their programme at Colorado Springs, gradually rebuilding fitness and improving his timings. The dip in form in the lead up to the CWG caused concern, but Gulveer trained hard for the event.“I only focus on giving my best. I worked on improving my fitness and timing. Also, I don’t keep track of my national records and all,” he had said.Before joining the 23 Grenadiers in 2018, Gulveer had never dreamt of becoming an international athlete. “I started running seriously after joining the Army. Before that, I used to run only to get enrolled. I didn’t know anything about the CWG or Asian Games. I only came to know about them after joining the Army. ”His life changed almost accidentally in 2019. Stationed in Arunachal Pradesh, Gulveer prepared seriously for an inter-unit cross-country race, hoping a good performance would earn incentives and provide respite from demanding military duties. His 10km victory in 30:58 caught the eye of Army Sports Institute coach Younus Khan, who brought him to Pune and transformed a soldier into India’s premier distance runner.That mindset was evident in Glasgow. Amid rain, the reigning Asian 5,000m and 10,000m champion judged the pace superbly, adding another medal to a kitty that already boast of an Asian Games bronze and Asian Championship double gold.
Article Summary: Gulveer Singh won silver at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 28-year-old became the first Indian runner to break the four-minute mile barrier. The reigning Asian 5,000m and 10,000M champion judged the pace superbly.

Why this could be one of his toughest Commonwealth Games competitions

NEW DELHI: Neeraj Chopra walks into the Commonwealth Games 2026 as India’s biggest athletics hope, but this may be far from a routine title defence.The Olympic champion and former world champion is returning to the Games after an eight-year gap, and the men’s javelin field in Glasgow is significantly stronger than the one he conquered in Gold Coast in 2018.Back then, Neeraj won gold with an 86.47m throw and looked a class apart. This time, he enters Scotstoun Stadium with questions around form, fitness and the depth of the competition. He missed Birmingham 2022 due to injury, and his 2026 season only began recently after recovering from a back problem.His first outing of the year at the Doha Diamond League showed both promise and rust. Neeraj produced a best throw of 85.69m, briefly moved into medal contention, but eventually finished fourth after two foul throws.For an athlete whose standards are now measured in 88m-plus and 90m territory, Doha suggested he is not yet at his absolute peak.The most obvious threat is Pakistan’s Arshad Nadeem. The rivalry between Neeraj and Arshad has become one of the defining stories in world athletics. Arshad owns a personal best of 92.97m, one of the greatest throws in history. His listed season best is only 78.47m, but that number is misleading because he has competed sparingly and has repeatedly shown he can produce huge throws in major championships.Grenada’s Anderson Peters is arguably the most dangerous athlete in the field on current form. The two-time world champion has a personal best of 93.07m and a season best of 86.38m, slightly better than Neeraj’s. Peters is known for his ability to throw consistently over 85m, which is often enough to stay in medal contention throughout a competition.Then there is Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, the emerging force of the field. At just 23, he arrives with a personal and season best of 92.62m, making him statistically one of the biggest threats to gold. Unlike some rivals whose best marks came years ago, Rumesh has already crossed 92m this season.India also has Rohit Yadav, who has thrown 87.05m, while experienced names such as Keshorn Walcott (90.16m PB) and Julius Yego (92.72m PB) add further quality to the competition.The biggest challenge for Neeraj is not just one rival; it is the number of athletes capable of throwing beyond 85m. In 2018, he was clearly ahead of the field. In Glasgow, at least five athletes have personal bests above 90m, and several have season marks within touching distance of his own.Another factor is timing. Neeraj is still building rhythm after a back injury, and javelin is an event where technical sharpness matters as much as physical strength. A small loss of timing at release can cost two or three metres, which could be the difference between gold and bronze in a field this deep.The format also adds pressure. Qualification is on Thursday, with the final in the early hours of August 1 (IST). Athletes must manage recovery, rhythm and conditions across two rounds, and one poor series can end a medal challenge quickly.Neeraj remains the favourite because of his championship temperament. He has repeatedly delivered under pressure at the Olympics, World Championships and Asian Games. But unlike Gold Coast 2018, this will not be a competition he can win by reputation alone.If he throws 88m or more, a second Commonwealth gold is very likely. If he stays around the 85-86m range seen in Doha, Glasgow could turn into one of the most competitive and unpredictable javelin finals of his career.
Article Summary: Olympic champion and former world champion is returning to the Games after an eight-year gap. His first outing of the year at the Doha Diamond League showed both promise and rust. The most obvious threat is Pakistan’s Arshad Nadeem, who owns a personal best of 92.97m.

Article Title: CWG 2026: India’s jumpers overcome absence of regular trainers
Article Text:
Murali Sreeshankar (Image credit: PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s jumpers have emerged among the standout performers in athletics at the Commonwealth Games, but their impressive results have come despite the absence of their coaches.High jumper Sarvesh Kushare clinched silver, while long jumpers Murali Sreeshankar and Lokesh Sathyanathan progressed to the final. High jumper Adarsh Ram finished fifth. Yet, throughout the competition, jumpers have largely been without their Indian coaches, who train them on a daily basis and guide them during competitions.Sarvesh’s coach Jithin Thomas is currently overseeing the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) training camp in Spala, Poland, which runs until Sept ahead of the Asian Games. Adarsh’s coach Sahana Kumari is with the Indian U-20 team for the World Athletics U-20 Championships in Eugene starting early next month. Sreeshankar’s father and coach, S Murali, a constant presence during his competitions, was not cleared to accompany him to Glasgow.The lack of dedicated coaching support became evident during the men’s high jump final. After withdrawing with a knee injury during the warm-up, Tejaswin Shankar stayed back to help Sarvesh from the sidelines.Noticing Sarvesh struggling with his approach, Tejaswin suggested a change in his run-up, advice that helped the eventual silver medallist regain rhythm. Tejaswin, himself, however, had no coach to support him through his own injury setback.According to the final athletics contingent cleared by the govt, chief coach Radhakrishnan Nair is the only Indian support staff personnel accredited with the contingent. The four foreign coaches accompanying the team are Scott Simmons (long distance), Jason Alexander Dawson (400m and relays), Ronald Gerd Weigel (race walking) and Yoandris Betanzos Francis (jumps).However, both Weigel and Betanzos have travelled as Extra Team Officials (ETOs), an accreditation that does not permit access to the competition venue and field of play. As a result, Betanzos can only watch the event from the stands and interact with athletes outside the venue, leaving India’s jumpers effectively without technical guidance during competition despite their strong performances.Raosaheb Jadhav, Sarvesh Kushare’s childhood coach, said, “Forget a coach, not a single support staff member was near the three Indian jumpers. All the other 15 jumpers had a coach or support staff member to correct their mistakes. During his two failed attempts, Sarvesh’s lower back touched the bar. Had there been a coach, he could have spotted the mistake on video and corrected it. Sarvesh could then have cleared 2.28m on his second attempt and won the gold. ”(inputs by Amit Sampat)
Article Summary: High jumper Sarvesh Kushare clinched silver, while long jumpers Murali Sreeshankar and Lokesh Sathyanathan progressed to the final. Yet, throughout the competition, jumpers have largely been without their Indian coaches, who train them on a daily basis and guide them during competitions.

Article Title: ICC unveils 12 venues for ODI World Cup 2027 as Africa hosts showpiece after 24 years

The International Cricket Council (ICC) on Thursday officially unveiled the 12 host venues for the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027, confirming the cities across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia that will stage the 50-over showpiece when it returns to Africa for the first time in 24 years.The announcement was made during a grand ceremony in Johannesburg, where the ICC also revealed the tournament's official brand identity, 'Three Nations, One Heartbeat', symbolising the shared spirit of optimism, diversity and unity among the three co-hosts.The 14th edition of the World Cup will feature 57 matches and 14 teams, with eight cities in South Africa, three in Zimbabwe, and Namibia's capital Windhoek selected as host venues.The tournament marks Africa's first Men's ODI World Cup since the 2003 edition, which was jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.ICC chairman Jay Shah described the venue announcement as a major milestone on the road to the global tournament."This marks an exciting milestone on the road to the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027. The unveiling of the host cities and the tournament brand signals the start of a journey that will unite fans around the world and build anticipation for one of our sport's biggest global events," he said.Shah also highlighted the significance of bringing cricket's flagship ODI tournament back to Africa."The return of this prestigious tournament to Africa after 24 years is a landmark moment for cricket. We are confident that South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia will deliver an unforgettable event, showcasing the warmth, passion and rich diversity that make this region truly unique," he added.ICC chief executive Sanjog Gupta said the event would celebrate both cricket and the continent's unique identity."The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup represents the legacy and spectacle of Limited Overs Cricket," he said. "It also marks the return of the pinnacle event to Africa after more than two decades and will celebrate a continent defined by extraordinary people, vibrant cultures, breathtaking experiences and deep love for Sport."Gupta added that the tournament's vibrant branding reflects the energy of the host nations while inspiring future generations of fans.The 2027 edition will be built around the African philosophy of 'Ubuntu' — "I am, because we are" — and the campaign theme 'Make the Circle Bigger', celebrating compassion, togetherness and cultural diversity across the region's 29 officially recognised languages.The tournament logo draws inspiration from the traditional African wire bowl, while its colour palette includes shades such as Zimbabwe Chilli, African Root, Fynbos Pop, Namib Dune, Harare Dawn and Two Oceans.The 2027 edition will feature a three-stage competition format.It will feature 57 matches and a three-stage format designed to increase competitiveness. Teams ranked 12th to 14th will first compete in a Super Series, with the winner advancing to the main tournament.The next stage will feature 12 teams split into two groups of six, each playing a round-robin. The top three teams from each group, along with the best fourth-placed side, will qualify for the Super 7. After 21 Super 7 matches, the top four teams will advance to the semi-finals before the final determines the champions.The launch ceremony was attended by several cricketing greats, including Graeme Smith, Makhaya Ntini, Hashim Amla, Temba Bavuma, Kagiso Rabada, Hamilton Masakadza and Rudolf Jansen van Vuuren, as anticipation officially began for cricket's biggest 50-over spectacle returning to African soil.
Article Summary: ICC unveils 12 host venues for ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027. Announcement made during a grand ceremony in Johannesburg. ICC also revealed the tournament's official brand identity, 'Three Nations, One Heartbeat' The tournament marks Africa's first Men's ODI World Cup since 2003.

Article Title: Future India captain? Selector explains why 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was named East Zone vice-captain
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Selectors back Sooryavanshi despite criticism

NEW DELHI: The decision to name 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi as East Zone vice-captain for the upcoming Duleep Trophy has raised eyebrows across the cricketing world, but the selectors believe they are investing in the future of Indian cricket.With experienced wicketkeeper-batter Ishan Kishan appointed captain, Sooryavanshi's elevation as deputy is not being viewed as an immediate leadership burden but as an opportunity to accelerate his development as a cricketer.One member of the East Zone selection committee explained the thinking behind the move, saying the teenager was not being handed the captaincy but was being prepared for greater responsibilities in the future."He has not been made the captain. He has only been made the vice-captain. The captain is Ishan Kishan. Besides, Ishan is a wicketkeeper, so he will be actively involved throughout the day. It is not as though Vaibhav will be captaining the team all day. As he grows, he is maturing day by day. Giving him more responsibility will help him mature even further," former Odisha Ranji player and selector Pravanjan Mullick told Cricbuzz.Mullick revealed that the selectors' decision was based on Sooryavanshi's rapid rise and his ability to handle responsibility despite his age."This is a great opportunity for him to take on the responsibility of being vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy. He wants to do well for the country, and we believe giving young players responsibility is important. Who knows? We are keeping our fingers crossed that one day he could even become India's captain. That is the thought behind giving him the vice-captaincy," he told Cricbuzz.The selectors also considered Sooryavanshi's previous leadership experience. The teenage batter has already served as vice-captain of Bihar in first-class cricket and was part of India's leadership group during the Under-19 World Cup triumph."He has been doing very well for the country and also had an excellent IPL season with Rajasthan Royals . He is also the vice-captain of Bihar in first-class cricket," Mullick said.The 15-year-old has enjoyed a meteoric rise over the last year. He became one of the youngest players to feature in the IPL and went on to top the batting charts during the tournament, earning widespread praise for his fearless approach. He was also named Player of the Series during India's tour of Zimbabwe.The East Zone selection committee meeting was held at Eden Gardens, with representatives from the Cricket Association of Bengal, Jharkhand State Cricket Association, Tripura Cricket Association, Bihar Cricket Association and Odisha Cricket Association taking part.Mullick clarified that there was no discussion with Sooryavanshi before the decision was made."No, none at all. It was a collective decision taken by all the selectors from the eastern states. He has the ability to handle responsibility and is capable of leading the team when required," he said.The selector also highlighted the importance of the Duleep Trophy as an opportunity for Sooryavanshi to impress national selectors."More importantly, this is a great opportunity for him to score runs. If he performs well in the Duleep Trophy, the national selectors will certainly be watching him. You never know, he could be in contention for the Indian Test team sooner rather than later," Mullick added.Addressing criticism over the appointment, Mullick said the selectors respected different opinions but stood by their decision."With due respect to everyone expressing their views, they are entitled to their opinions. Everyone has a right to think differently, and we cannot change that. But we did what we believed was best for the team. It was a collective decision," he said.East Zone, featuring players like Mohammed Shami, Mukesh Kumar, Shahbaz Ahmed and Abhimanyu Easwaran, will begin their Duleep Trophy campaign against North Zone in Bengaluru on August 23.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi named East Zone vice-captain for upcoming Duleep Trophy. 15-year-old has enjoyed a meteoric rise over the last year. He became one of the youngest players to feature in the IPL and went on to top the batting charts during the tournament.

NEW DELHI: Ajinkya Rahane's decision to retire from international cricket on Thursday triggered an outpouring of tributes from some of Indian sport's biggest names, with Sachin Tendulkar leading the emotional farewell by recalling the qualities that defined the veteran batter's remarkable career.Rahane, who represented India in 85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is between 2011 and 2023, brought the curtain down on an international career highlighted by his calm leadership during India's historic 2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy triumph in Australia.Among the many messages, Tendulkar's stood out for its personal touch, having shared both the Mumbai dressing room and the crease with Rahane early in his career."Congratulations on a remarkable career, @ajinkyarahane88. The first time we batted together for Mumbai, I saw someone who never chased moments. They came to you because you were willing to do the hard yards for the team," Tendulkar wrote on X.Reflecting on Rahane's defining captaincy stint in Australia, the batting legend added: "That same quality defined your finest hour in Australia. You showed that composure isn't the opposite of aggression. It is often what gives a team the confidence to be fearless.Congratulations on a wonderful career! Wishing you and your family all the very best."Tendulkar was at the other end when Rahane made his Test debut against Australia in Delhi in 2013, encouraging the youngster to embrace the occasion.Former India head coach Ravi Shastri, under whom Rahane enjoyed many of his biggest Test successes, also paid tribute to the veteran batter."One of India's most committed cricketers who was an integral part of my tenure as coach and gave yeoman service to Mumbai and Indian cricket. Well done Jinks."Rahane's finest chapter came under Shastri's coaching when he stepped in for Virat Kohli after the Adelaide Test in 2020 and led an injury-ravaged Indian side to a memorable 2-1 series victory in Australia, including the famous triumph at the Gabba.Cheteshwar Pujara congratulated his long-time batting partner on "a career you can be incredibly proud of," saying it had been an honour sharing countless partnerships and memories with him.The BCCI thanked Rahane for his "immense contribution to Indian cricket and all the memories that will be cherished forever."Former opener Virender Sehwag described Rahane as "one of the most underrated cricketers" and hailed him as "the man who led India to its greatest ever overseas Test series win," adding that he "never made any noise and kept giving his best."Shikhar Dhawan remembered Rahane as a composed leader and dependable teammate, while former all-rounder Irfan Pathan thanked him for creating "outstanding Australian memories."Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu also joined the tributes, recalling Rahane's memorable 103 at Lord's in 2014, calling it an innings of "immense character and class."Rahane retires with 5,077 Test runs, including 12 centuries, and an unbeaten record as India's Test captain, having registered four wins and two draws in six matches. His calm leadership, resilience under pressure and ability to deliver in overseas conditions remain defining features of a career that earned widespread respect across the cricketing world.
Article Summary: Sachin Tendulkar pays tribute to Ajinkya Rahane on Twitter. Rahane retires with 5,077 Test runs, including 12 centuries, and an unbeaten record as India's Test captain. The batsman represented India in 85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is between 2011 and 2023.

Article Title: 'Few boxes to tick': Josh Hazlewood eyes BGT win in India, Ashes in England before retirement

Australia fast bowler Josh Hazlewood has set his sights on winning Test series in South Africa, India and England as the team prepares for a busy schedule over the next 12 months.Australia are scheduled to play at least 20 Tests during this period, including away series in South Africa, India and the Ashes in England.Hazlewood, 35, has played 76 Tests but has never been part of an Australian team that won a Test series in India or England. Australia last won an away Ashes series in 2001, while their last Test series win in India came in 2004."This group's been together for quite a long time now, the majority of it, anyway," Hazlewood said, as quoted by Cricbuzz. I haven't won in South Africa either, so there's three that are coming up that are a few boxes to tick off there for not just me but from this whole playing group.""I guess that's been a driving factor during this prep, sort of in the back of your head, and even the months leading into it. Tough competition, and hopefully we get the job done."Hazlewood is also hoping to return to the Test side after missing the Ashes last summer because of hamstring and Achilles injuries. If selected, it will be his first Test in 13 months, the longest gap of his career between Test appearances.He could compete with Scott Boland for the third fast bowler's place in the playing XI. Chief selector George Bailey has previously indicated that Boland has closed the gap in the race for selection.Hazlewood said he would like to play more Tests alongside Boland, who has often missed out whenever Australia's three first-choice fast bowlers have all been available.“I think [Boland and I have] only played one game together – at Edgbaston [in the 2023 Ashes] – and I'd love to play more with Scotty," Hazlewood said. Article Title: Stephen Fleming takes over as England Test coach; former CSK boss begins new era with Joe Root
Article Text:
Stephen Fleming (ANI Photo)

Fleming eager to build on England's foundations

Root and ECB back new partnership



Former Chennai Super Kings (CSK) head coach and New Zealand great Stephen Fleming has been appointed as England men's Test head coach, with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) confirming one of the biggest coaching moves in world cricket.The 53-year-old replaces fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum , who stepped down from the Test role after England's series defeat to New Zealand in June, although he continues to oversee the white-ball teams.Fleming will officially begin his tenure later this summer after spending time with his family in New Zealand. Marcus Trescothick will remain interim coach for the upcoming Test series against Pakistan before Fleming takes charge ahead of England's tour of South Africa.The appointment also marks a reunion with Joe Root , who returns as England's Test captain after replacing the retired Ben Stokes.Despite never coaching an international side before, Fleming arrives with one of the strongest coaching resumes in franchise cricket.He spent 18 years with CSK, guiding the franchise to five IPL titles and 10 finals, while also coaching Southern Brave in The Hundred, Melbourne Stars in the Big Bash League, and CSK's affiliated teams in South Africa and the United States.As a player, Fleming captained New Zealand in a record 80 Tests, winning 28 matches, and remains one of the country's greatest Test leaders.Speaking after his appointment, Fleming said he was honoured to take charge of one of cricket's biggest jobs."I'm incredibly excited to be joining England as Test Coach. It's one of the most prestigious coaching positions in world cricket, and I am honoured to be appointed," he said.He added that England's immediate ambition would remain winning matches while ensuring the team continues to develop for the future."The ambition is always to win now. But equally, it's about ensuring the team is well placed for the medium and long-term future. There is a lot of young talent in and around the team and our aim is to help them fulfil their potential as world-class cricketers," he added.Fleming also welcomed the opportunity to work alongside returning skipper Root."I'm particularly looking forward to working with Joe Root as Captain... There is still plenty more to come from him," Fleming said.He also identified Harry Brook 's development as a key priority, adding: "The best players are never finished products."Reflecting on his long association with English cricket, Fleming said: "English cricket gave that to me, and it is a privilege to have this chance to give something back."Root described his return as England captain as "a great honour and privilege" and said working with Fleming was a major reason for accepting the role again."The opportunity to do that alongside Stephen is also a huge motivator. He has proved over a long period of time that he is an exceptional leader with a great knowledge of the game," he said.ECB managing director Rob Key called Fleming "one of the most highly respected figures in cricket" and said he believes the New Zealander can turn England's talented squad into "a world-class outfit" capable of sustained success.England currently sit seventh in the World Test Championship standings, and Fleming's arrival signals the start of a fresh chapter as they attempt to rebuild their red-ball fortunes.
Article Summary: Stephen Fleming has been appointed as England men's Test head coach. The 53-year-old replaces Brendon McCullum, who stepped down after England's series defeat to New Zealand in June. Fleming will officially begin his tenure later this summer after spending time with his family in New Zealand.

Article Title: Ajinkya Rahane was a ‘man for the crisis’, an ideal batsman for SENA countries
Article Text:
India's Ajinkya Rahane (Photo by AP/PTI)

Poll Vote & Share your view What role do you think Ajinkya Rahane should take up after retirement? Commentator Cricket analyst 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: An era concluded in Indian cricket as Ajinkya Rahane announced his retirement from all forms of cricket on Thursday. The former India captain, who famously led the side to a remarkable Test series triumph in Australia in 2020-21, made the announcement in an emotional post on social media on Thursday.Rahane walks off having featured in 85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is for India while also turning out in 212 IPL games for six teams. He put out a video statement on his Instagram account making his decision public, where he said: "The reality of life is that everything has a beginning and everything has an end. When the time comes, we simply have to respect it and move forward. I have always relied on timing in my batting and I have always understood its importance. Today, I feel the timing is right for me to move on and announce my retirement from international cricket and all formats."Paying rich compliments to Rahane, former India skipper Dilip Vengsarkar, who has closely observed Rahane's career over the years, told TOI, "I've seen Ajinkya since his Under-19 days. At that time, I was the chairman of the BCCI's talent spotters (TRDO). He was also a part of the India Emerging team for a tour of Australia (in 2008).He was a hard-working, focused, disciplined and sincere cricketer. Of course, the highlights of his career were scoring that match-winning century for India at Lord's (against England in 2014 in a Test) and captaining India to an amazing series win in Australia in the 2020-21 (Border-Gavaskar) Test series. "However, Vengsarkar felt that India's think tank could've treated Rahane better. "But the one thing I didn't understand, that after captaining India to a Test win against Australia at Dharmashala (in March 2017), how did he become the 12th man just six months later? It was baffling to see at that time," the ex-chairman of selectors wondered. Vengsarkar was referring to India's tour of South Africa in 2018, when Rahane was dropped for the first two Tests at Cape Town and Centurion, before being recalled for the third Test at Johannesburg.Praising Rahane's technique, Vengsarkar said, "He had a very good technique and temperament. He also had a good defensive technique in the longest format of the game. He was one of our best batters in overseas conditions, and a good player of fast bowling. The only thing is that I wish he had a continuous stint as an India cricketer, because that also helps the player mentally. Being in and out of the side continuously is detrimental to the confidence of a cricketer, and his game was all about confidence. ""Ajinkya conducted himself very well off the field as well. He played for Mumbai with the same intensity and commitment as he did for India. I wish him all the best for his future endeavors post retirement. It's a good, expected decision by Rahane. Possibly he wants to build a career in media," Vengsarkar felt.Former India batter Pravin Amre , who was the Mumbai head coach when Rahane made his first-class debut back in Sept 2007 for Mumbai against Karachi Urban in the Mohammad Nissar Trophy, said, “For me, I think it's been an incredible journey. I'm very proud of Rahane’s journey, because I saw him as an under-17 player. And from there, representing in 85 Tests, is truly phenomenal. Also, he played for 18 years in the IPL, which is incredible. He captained India’s Test team. Nobody can forget his contribution in Australia, especially when India lost the first Test at Adelaide, and then won the second Test at Melbourne. He led from the front with a century.”Amre rated Rahane’s century against Australia in the memorable 2020-21 Test series even higher than the batter’s classy ton at Lord’s on a greentop, which helped India win that Test against all odds.“As a coach, I enjoyed many of his milestones, like getting that Test century at Lord’s, which I think was one of the best centuries by an India batter in an overseas Test. It was a top-class knock on a complete great top. However, I will still rate his century in the (second Test) Melbourne Test (in 2020-21) higher. That hundred was about him leading from the front, as Virat was not there. I think that the course of that Test, and that series changed completely after his hundred,” Amre said.Amre asserted that it was Rahane’s ability to score centuries in tough conditions overseas, especially the SENA countries, that marked him out as special.“One is rated as a complete batsman when one scores runs in England, Australia, and the SENA countries in general. And Ajinkya did that. I think that was his main role, and that's what we (he and Rahane) prepared for also, and I'm proud of it. I definitely feel that Rahane deserved to play 100 Tests. However, he finished with a phenomenal record. His contribution as a fielder also was great, especially in the slips, he was brilliant,” Amre gushed.Praising the attitude of his ward and his ability to bat India out of crisis situations in tough conditions, Amre said, “Ajinkya was a coach's delight. To work with him was such a wonderful experience, because he was always willing to listen, which I think is very important. He enjoyed his cricket. He gave plenty of enjoyment to Team India’s fans as well, because whenever India needed him the most, he was there with the bat. He was India’s ‘Crisis Man.’ That's what's very important. It wasn’t easy for him since he played in an Indian team which had great players like Rohit (Sharma) and Virat (Kohli). The limelight was not on him. However, he played his role of a reliable Test batsman perfectly.”Pointing out that Rahane was also a good limited-overs player, Amre said, “People underestimated his white-ball game. If you see, anybody who played 18 years of IPL is a phenomenal achievement. I saw his entire journey. We worked together. I am proud of his commitment, his performances under pressure.”Amre felt that Rahane could contribute a lot to the game after his retirement. “I wish him all the best for a good second innings. And that’s because he can be a good coach or a commentator. But I want him to be connected with cricket. Because now he is an experienced man. And you cannot buy experience in the supermarket.”“I was there when he made his debut for Mumbai, in Pakistan, and scored a century (143). It was something special. He always enjoyed pressure. He is a quiet warrior. He never showed off. As a coach, I can say that he has performed to his potential. I’m proud of his achievement, and whenever he was given an opportunity, he gave his best. That is more important,” concluded Amre.After waiting on the bench for 16 Tests, Rahane finally made his Test debut in the home series against Australia in Delhi in the fourth and final Test in March 2013. India won that match by six wickets, but Rahane failed miserably, as he was dismissed for 7 & 1. However, the Mumbai batter bounced back from that initial setback, slamming a magnificent century (103) at Lord’s against England in July 2014 to shape India’s stunning 95-run win on a greentop.Subsequently, he went on to establish himself as one of the crucial cogs of India's batting spine for years to come. Rahane played 85 Tests, scoring 5,077 runs at an average of 38.46. The 38-year-old played his last Test at Port of Spain against West Indies in July 2023, after making a comeback for the World Test Championship final against Australia at the Oval a month earlier. However, he found himself sidelined due to poor form and the selectors’ will to look beyond him. In March 2024, he captained Mumbai to their 42nd Ranji Trophy title. He expressed a willingness to return to India’s Test team for one last time, but his lack of runs in domestic cricket for Mumbai didn’t support his cause.During his illustrious career, Rahane became one of India’s most reliable middle-order batters away from home, where he scored eight of his 12 Test tons, with one each coming in England and New Zealand and two each in Sri Lanka and West Indies."From those early days traveling from Dombivli as a young boy just to practice, I gave this game everything I had. Every single day, every innings, every opportunity I got to bat, the dream was always to wear the India cap. I lived by one simple rule: always put my country and my team ahead of myself. I played this game with complete honesty and I have always believed that if your intent is right, the game will always take care of you. Since the time I made my debut as a first-class cricketer, Indian cricket has grown tremendously and I feel so proud to have been a part of it over the last 20 years. While my chapter as an Indian cricketer comes to an end, my journey with the game doesn't.""I look forward to helping the next generation, sharing the values this sport has taught me, and giving back to the game that has given me everything. From starting out as a young player in Mumbai, to playing for India, it has been an absolute honor. There have been many wins and losses along the way, but the sheer joy of playing cricket, being part of different teams, and creating lifelong memories, that has been the greatest satisfaction of my career. To the BCCI, the MCA, my teammates, my coaches, every IPL franchise, to Radhika, my entire family, my friends, and everyone who stood by me, thank you."And a very special thank you to all the cricket fans who supported me through every high and low. Ajinkya means unbeatable, but cricket has shown me defeat many times. As cricketers, we fail more often than we succeed. My team has lost matches, I have made mistakes, but there is one place where I was never defeated, and that was in your hearts. (In Marathi) You always treated me like your own. Thank you for your love, your faith, and your support. Cap number 278, signing off," said Rahane in is video message.Reacting to Rahane’s decision, Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) president Ajinkya Naik said, "Ajinkya Rahane’s retirement marks the end of a remarkable chapter in Indian cricket. His dedication, composure under pressure, and commitment to excellence have made him one of Mumbai cricket’s finest ambassadors. His legacy will inspire generations to come."
Article Summary: Former India captain Ajinkya Rahane retires from all forms of cricket. Rahane played 85 Tests, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is for India while also turning out in 212 IPL games for six teams. He famously led the side to a remarkable Test series triumph in Australia in 2020-21.

Yet, numbers only tell part of his story."The reality of life is that everything has a beginning, and everything has an end. When that time comes, you simply have to respect it and move forward. I always relied on timing in my batting, and I've always understood its important," Rahane said in his retirement video.If there is one chapter that defines Rahane's legacy, it is India's remarkable 2020-21 Test series win in Australia.After India were bowled out for 36 in Adelaide and Virat Kohli returned home on paternity leave, few believed the injury-hit side could compete, let alone win.Rahane stepped in as captain and led a depleted Indian team to a stunning 2-1 series victory, one of the greatest triumphs in Indian cricket history.His century in the Boxing Day Test at Melbourne not only rescued India's campaign but also made him the only Indian to score a Boxing Day Test hundred against Australia both as a player and as captain.Under his leadership, India never lost a Test match, making his captaincy record (6 matches with 4 wins and 2 draws) one of the finest in Indian cricket.Rahane earned a reputation for producing his best performances away from home. He became the first Indian batter to score both his maiden Test and ODI centuries in SENA countries, proving his ability to thrive in the toughest conditions.His 12 Test hundreds often came in pressure situations, and remarkably, India never lost a Test whenever Rahane scored a century. He was also the first Indian to score a century in the World Test Championship, adding another milestone to an already impressive career.One of his finest individual performances came against South Africa when he became the only Indian batter to score centuries in both innings of a Test while batting at No. 5 or lower.Rahane's contributions extended beyond the bat. He remains the only Indian fielder to take eight catches in a Test match, highlighting his exceptional reflexes in the slips.Earlier in his career, he also announced himself in T20Is by scoring 61 on debut, the highest score by an Indian on T20I debut at the time.Despite falling out of the national team, Rahane continued to contribute in domestic cricket. He led Mumbai to their record-extending 42nd Ranji Trophy title in the 2023-24 season, showing that his leadership qualities remained intact.Rahane's retirement message reflected the humility that defined his career."From those early days, travelling from Dombivali as a young boy, just to practice, I gave this game everything I had. Every single day, every innings, every opportunity I got to bat, the dream was always to wear the India cap."He also underlined the values that shaped him as a cricketer."I lived by one single rule, only support my country and my team ahead of myself. I played this game with complete honesty, and I always believe that if your intent is right, the game will always take care of you."Looking ahead, Rahane made it clear his association with cricket is far from over."While my chapter, as an Indian cricketer, comes to an end, my journey with the game doesn't. I look forward to helping the next generation, sharing the values, the sport has taught me, and giving back to the game that has given me everything."Perhaps the most emotional part of his farewell came when he reflected on failure and resilience. He said, "Ajinkya means unbeatable. But cricket has shown me defeat many times. As cricketers, we fail more often, then we succeed."He signed off with a message that perfectly summed up his relationship with Indian fans."My team has lost matches. I have made mistakes, but there is one place where I was never defeated, and that was in your heart. You always treated me like your own. Thank you for your love. Your faith, and your support. Cap number 278, signing off."

Saltburn Cricket Club have suspended a player, humorously called "Clicky Ponting", after he was accused of cheating during a local league match by clicking his fingers to make it sound like the batter had edged the ball.The incident, which happened during Saltburn’s second XI win over Norton, went viral on social media after video footage appeared to show the fielder making the sound just before the wicketkeeper completed the catch.The umpire gave the batter out, sparking widespread criticism online.Responding to the controversy, Saltburn Cricket Club, an English outfit, said they were taking the allegations seriously and had suspended the player while an investigation is underway.In a statement, the club said, “We are treating this allegation with the utmost seriousness and, as a family-centric club, we are fully cooperating with the NYS League’s investigation.”The statement added, “The player at the centre of the complaint has been suspended and will not play again for the club this season or in the foreseeable future, pending the outcome of this investigation.”Saltburn have also withdrawn from their second-team cup match against Marton as the investigation continues.Club officials have already spoken with league representatives and said the situation has been difficult for everyone involved.They added, “This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club entirely run by volunteers.”The viral clip has now been viewed more than 7.5 million times on X, with several well-known figures criticising the alleged act.

Article Title: 'Conditions not best for javelin throwers': Neeraj Chopra after reaching CWG 2026 final - WATCH

NEW DELHI: Neeraj Chopra qualified for the men's javelin throw final at the Commonwealth Games 2026 despite difficult weather conditions in Glasgow. After finishing fifth in the qualification round with a best throw of 79.61m, the Olympic champion said the cold and changing winds made it tough for all athletes.However, he was happy that all three Indian javelin throwers reached the final.Neeraj did enough to secure his place in the 12-man final with a best throw of 79.61m at Scotstoun Stadium. In the gold medal match, he will compete against defending Commonwealth champion Arshad Nadeem, Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, world champion Keshorn Walcott and former world champion Anderson Peters.India's Rohit Yadav and Yash Vir Singh also qualified, giving India three medal hopes in the final.Neeraj said he was not looking for a huge throw in the qualification round. His main aim was to book a place in the final.“It was really cold and windy, but the throw was okay, the 79m throw. The goal was to go in the final and give my best in the final, so I'm happy with the throw,” Neeraj said.“Conditions are not best for javelin throwers. Not only cold, but it's really windy. The wind was also not in the front; sometimes it's from the side.It's really hard to process where we have to throw. Sometimes we think, ‘Okay, we'll throw there’, but then the wind comes from the other side. And lots of throwers are struggling today. Nobody touched the automatic qualification mark. It was tough conditions, but we are happy that all three Indians are in the final,” he said.Neeraj believes the final will be of a very high standard as several top javelin throwers from around the world will be competing for medals.“Yeah, it's a crazy field. For an event like Javelin Throw, that will be a really good final. Hope conditions will be okay tomorrow. Everyone looks in good shape. Let's see tomorrow.”Neeraj also praised Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, calling him one of the brightest young talents in the sport. He said it is good to see javelin becoming more popular in South Asia.“He's the new kid on the block, the rising star. He throws really well. He's a good friend of mine. This year he has thrown really well. It's good that Javelin is growing in our neighbourhood. It feels good that he did something great for Sri Lanka.”Neeraj said javelin has become much more popular in recent years. Better coaching, improved facilities and easy access to training information have helped young athletes take up the sport.“Javelin is really popular in South Asia now. There are lots of Javelin throwers. There are lots of athletes, and they are training for Javelin. So there is a better chance that so many good athletes will come. Earlier, Javelin as a sport was not that famous. But in the last few years, people support javelin and people know about the sport. So they know there is a future, and they really push themselves.“We have good facilities now, and we know about javelin. Because when I started, I didn't know how we had to plan for Javelin training and how we had to train. But right now, because of the internet, you can know about Javelin training. So it's really good that people know about Javelin now. That's why people recognise Javelin throw, and they try to give their best.”Neeraj said winning the gold medal at the Tokyo Olympics helped increase interest in javelin across India. He added that the country now has many athletes capable of throwing beyond 80 metres.“Earlier, there were lots of other really good athletes that provided a boost to other sports. But after my Tokyo Olympics gold, there was an immense boost in Javelin. I'm happy we have really good throwers now. I think we have around 20 80m throwers, so it’s really good for India,” Chopra concluded.

He will compete against defending Commonwealth champion Arshad Nadeem, Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage and world champion Keshorn Walcott.

Article Title: Dinesh Kumar's record-breaking form lifts Commonwealth Games expectations
Article Text:
Indian cyclist Dinesh Kumar

Just days before boarding the flight to Glasgow for Commonwealth Games, Indian cyclist Dinesh Kumar sent out a timely reminder of his form by breaking his own national record once again.The Indian Air Force rider clocked 4:39.118 in the men's 4,000m individual pursuit at the selection trials, shaving nearly three seconds off his previous national record. He heads into his second Commonwealth Games with renewed confidence, where he will compete in the individual pursuit on Friday.After finishing 19th in the team pursuit on his Games debut in Birmingham in 2022, the 27-year-old believes he is in a much better place this time around.“I have prepared really well and will try to give my best,” Dinesh told TOI before leaving for Glasgow. “I definitely feel I can do much better than last time.”That confidence has been built over the past month and a half in Kazakhstan, where he trained at high altitude under coach Maxat Ayazbayev. The camp, based in Almaty, was designed with both the Commonwealth Games and next year’s Asian Games in mind.“We had just returned three days before the trials,” he said. “The weather there was very good. It wasn’t too hot and the conditions were ideal for training. High-altitude training helps a lot because when we come back down, our body adapts better to the oxygen levels.”Sadly, only two of India’s endurance cyclists — Dinesh and Harshveer Singh Sekhon — will be competing in Glasgow, while there will be four from the sprint squad and they continued their preparations in Delhi.For Dinesh, cycling has always been more than a sport. Growing up in Rourkela, he first picked up the bicycle during school competitions before earning selection to SAI academy in Delhi in 2015. But the spark came even earlier.“There was a senior rider from Rourkela named Parasuram. Watching him inspired me to take up cycling,” he recalled.More than a decade later, Dinesh is among India’s leading track cyclists, balancing elite sport with his job in the Indian Air Force, which he joined in 2017.Behind every international trip lies another challenge that most people never see — travelling with equipment worth nearly Rs. 18 lakhs. Dinesh carries at least two bicycles to every major competition and this time it will be a Rs.10 lakh track bike and a Rs.8 lakh road bike.“We remove the wheels and handlebars, pack them and carry them ourselves. It takes around 10 minutes. It’s part of our job, so we don’t really worry about it,” he said. A mechanic also accompanies the team to help assemble and service the bicycles during competitions.Despite representing India at the highest level, Dinesh, however, feels cycling still has a long way to go in Odisha. “States like Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Karnataka have many cyclists competing nationally and internationally,” he said. “Odisha is improving, but we still have some catching up to do.”His journey has not been entirely smooth. In 2018, Dinesh suffered a broken collarbone, an injury that could have derailed his career. Instead, he recovered, and won his first-ever cycling gold medal in the Under-21 30km individual event at 2020 Khelo India Youth Games in Guwahati.Now, with a fresh national record on his legs and weeks of high-altitude training to boost, Dinesh will hope his second Commonwealth Games turns out to be a significant improvement over his first campaign.
Article Summary: Dinesh Kumar will compete in the men's 4,000m individual pursuit on Friday. The 27-year-old finished 19th in the team pursuit on his Games debut in Birmingham in 2022. Dinesh has been training at high altitude in Kazakhstan for the past month and a half.

Article Title: Lisha Das's race derailed before it began: Administrative lapses overshadow CWG debut
Article Text:
Lisha Das

While 16-year-old para cyclist Lisha Das finished sixth and last in the women’s C4-C5 4,000m individual pursuit qualification at the Commonwealth Games on Thursday, the authorities must also shoulder part of the blame for the consistent mental harassment the minor athlete endured in the lead-up to her race. Her performance was below expectations, but it came after days of administrative uncertainty and fresh logistical setbacks that severely disrupted her preparations.Lisha’s support team travelled from India to Glasgow via Zurich on a Swiss Air flight after their tickets were booked at the last minute due to delays in securing accreditation for her coach and female support staff.During the Zurich transit, her customised bicycle, packed in specialised bike boxes along with essential racing equipment, failed to be loaded onto the connecting flight. Her coaching team, assisted by the Indian contingent’s chef de mission office, spent an entire day pursuing the airline before the equipment finally reached Glasgow just hours before her race on Thursday.Lisha’s troubles, however, did not end there. Although coach Aditya Verma received last-minute accreditation to watch her race from outside the field of play, her preferred female chaperone, Dr Asha Shaikh, was denied access to the competition venue, leaving the minor athlete without her chosen support person.Unable to rely on specialised assistance, Lisha had no choice but to forgo wearing her customised aerodynamic skinsuit, competing instead in a conventional jersey and bib shorts that she could manage independently. It is learnt that female coaches and support staff from rival teams helped her in the changing area with her racing attire.Inside the velodrome, technician K. Dattatreya was the only accredited Indian support member permitted in the coaching enclosure, while Verma watched from the stands. Battling mounting stress until race time, Lisha clocked 6:58.000 to finish sixth and last in qualification.Note: The only wording correction beyond punctuation is changing "discard wearing" to "forgo wearing", as "discard wearing" is not grammatically correct. Everything else has been preserved.

Article Title: Sreeshankar falls short of gold, claims back-to-back Commonwealth Games silver
Article Text:
Sreeshankar, of India, poses after winning the silver medal (AP Photo)

It was a bitter-sweet moment for Sreeshankar as he failed to take the top step of the podium, but he added a second straight silver medal to his collection from the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Wednesday.Walking away crestfallen after his sixth and final jump, Sreeshankar was comforted and congratulated by his dad and coach, S. Murali, and that brought some comfort. The star jumper said he was down since he was gunning for gold.Sreeshankar was in pole position till the fourth round before the Jamaican, Tajay Gayle, went ahead with his fourth leap that measured 8.15m.“I was disappointed, but then I was happy with another silver. The conditions were tough as it was the first time I was competing in such cold weather. It felt like around 10 degrees Celsius,” Sreeshankar told TOI from Glasgow.“My best jump could have been the fourth one. Those are minute mistakes which creep in,” said the jumper, who extended his run-up a bit from his normal approach of 45 metres.Sreeshankar’s final card read 8.03, 8.09, x, x, 7.94 and 7.97m.On fellow Indian Lokesh Sathyanathan’s show — he finished fifth with a best leap of 7.97m — Sreeshankar said, “We push each other to give our best and that helps.”Reviewing Sreeshankar’s performance, Murali rated his fourth jump, which turned out to be a narrow foul, as one of the best efforts by the Indian on Wednesday.“His best jump came in the trial jump. That should have been in the 8.20m range, but in the end it turned out to be a 1cm foul,” the coach said, referring to Sreeshankar overstepping the board.Murali said from Glasgow, “It could have very well been a golden day for India, but in the end, I’ll take it given the hardships we faced over the last two years.”Murali, who reached Glasgow following the special intervention of the Indian Olympic Association president, was glad that he made the trip.“His first jump, measured at 8.03m, should have been a big one as he took off from way behind the board. I think he left some 20cm on the board. Otherwise, it would have been an even better day for Indian athletics,” he said.
