Adopt them yourself, and see miracles unfold.On Wednesday, Dilip Gavit won gold in the men's T47 para 100m at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. But since Sunday, the Indian knew he was winning the race. And this was not about new-fangled notions of manifesting things beforehand. This was simple fact."My coach had told me that I was going to win gold. So, I was sure that I would win," Gavit told TOI afterwards.So sure, that it was of little consequence that the 23-year-old 400m specialist was running the 100m dash, simply because the Games didn't have a 400m event in his para category.So sure that he clocked a Games record time of 10.71s for his gold.It was one-two for India, with Kerala's Mohammed Basil Morssinganakth taking silver with 10.83s. The bronze went to England's Kevin Santos, who clocked 10.85s."I have a lot of faith in my coach, Vaijanath Kale. I know that if he says something, it will happen," he said. "This gold medal is my gift to my coach on Guru Purnima," added the native of Torandongri, a small tribal village near Nashik in Maharashtra.What Gavit doesn't realise is that it is the other way round. That belief and hope are a constant give and take.It all started with a small intuition sparked nine years ago, when Kale, a local coach in Nashik, saw Gavit running during a kho-kho game in his village. The coach saw potential in the young boy and asked him to train under him in Nashik. Son of farm workers, young Gavit didn't have the means to play a sport.Kale found a solution."I adopted him," the coach told TOI from Glasgow. It was as simple as that."I took permission from his parents, and I started taking care of him as a guardian formally," he added. "I saw a lot of potential in Dilip. He had lost his hand at a young age, but he was full of positivity and was competitive with able-bodied kids of his age."When he was just five, Gavit lost his right arm from the elbow downwards to gangrene. He fell from a tree while playing and was rushed to a local vaid (Ayurvedic doctor) for treatment."The local doctor just put a bandage on his hand and sent him home," the coach said. The untreated infection turned into gangrene, and by the time his parents took him to a hospital in Nashik, it was too late. Gavit's hand had to be amputated.But that severed arm has never proved a limitation for either the athlete or the coach."Coach sir has always fielded me with able-bodied competitors. I have never been made to feel that I lack something. Training and competing with them has made me stronger and more confident," said Gavit, who won 4x400m gold for Maharashtra at the Khelo India Youth Games (non-para) in Pune in 2019."The CWG didn't have a 400m event in his category, so I asked him to run in the 100m event," the coach explained.Kale, who runs a small real estate business in Nashik, trains more than a dozen athletes and has adopted four more boys from rural Maharashtra."I have the means to support their training and cost of living. My business gives me enough to support these five kids, and my family (sons and parents) supports me in this. My wife is a nutritionist and helps prepare their diet," he said.
Article Summary: Dilip Gavit won gold in the men's T47 para 100m at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 23-year-old lost his right arm from the elbow downwards to gangrene at the age of five. Coach Vaijanath Kale saw potential in the young boy and asked him to train under him in Nashik.

Article Title: 'Pakistan ke liye medal jeetu': Arshad Nadeem's message ahead of Neeraj Chopra showdown at CWG javelin final

Article Title: India at Commonwealth Games 2026 Day 8: Lovepreet’s silver, Seema’s bronze sparks pride; Neeraj books final spot
Article Text:

Seema claims bronze as Nidhi narrowly misses out

Tejaswin Shankar remains firmly in medal contention

Positive day sets up busy finish to the Games

India enjoyed another eventful day at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Thursday, collecting a silver and a bronze medal while several athletes advanced to finals across athletics and bowls, and others concluded their campaigns.Weightlifter Lovepreet Singh narrowly missed out on gold in the men's +110kg category before settling for silver, while Seema Kaliramna battled through a difficult women's discus throw final to secure bronze. Elsewhere, Tejaswin Shankar ended the opening day of the decathlon in medal contention, all three Indian javelin throwers progressed to the final, and both of the country's triple jump representatives also booked their places in the medal round.By the end of Day 8, India's overall medal tally stood at 17 medals (3 gold, 10 silver and 4 bronze).India's day began on the weightlifting platform with Lovepreet Singh producing one of the best performances of his career in the men's +110kg final.Lovepreet lifted 176kg in the snatch, setting a new Indian national record, before following it with another national record of 212kg in the clean and jerk. His combined total of 388kg earned him the silver medal, finishing just 1kg behind New Zealand's David Liti, who claimed gold.The result also capped India's weightlifting campaign with an eighth medal from the sport at the Glasgow Games.Later in the women's +86kg competition, Martina Devi Maibam narrowly missed out on a podium finish. She registered a combined lift of 245kg to finish fifth.India added another medal in athletics through Seema Kaliramna in the women's discus throw final.Her competition began with a foul before she recovered with a throw of 57.32m in the second round.Seema then produced the decisive effort of her evening with 58.65m on her third attempt. Although she fouled on each of her remaining three throws, that mark proved enough to secure the bronze medal.Jamaica's Samantha Hall won gold with 61.66m, while Canada's Julia Tunks took silver with 60.67m.India came close to celebrating a second medal in the event as Nidhi Rani steadily improved during the competition before recording a best effort of 57.10m. She ultimately finished fourth, narrowly missing the podium.India's strongest unfinished event came in the men's decathlon.After completing the opening day's five disciplines — the 100m, long jump, shot put, high jump and 400m — Tejaswin Shankar ended the day in second place with 4,339 points.He trails Olympic champion Damian Warner by only 14 points, leaving the medal race wide open ahead of Friday's concluding five events.There was encouraging news in the men's javelin qualification, where all three Indian athletes progressed. Neeraj Chopra qualified comfortably after producing a best throw of 79.61m, finishing fifth overall in qualifying.Rohit Yadav also advanced with 78.37m, placing ninth, while Yash Vir Singh completed India's clean sweep after qualifying in tenth with a throw of 78.36m.The trio will now compete together in the final.India also enjoyed a successful session in the men's triple jump qualifiers.Praveen Chithravel finished second overall to comfortably book his place in the final, while Selva Prabhu Thirumaran also advanced after finishing third in qualifying.Both athletes remain in contention for medals later in the competition.Not all of India's athletics results produced progression.In the men's shot put final, Tajinderpal Singh Toor finished fifth, while Samardeep Singh Gill placed sixth.On the track, Vishal TK failed to qualify for the men's 400m final, while Animesh Kujur also missed out on a place in the men's 200m final.Parul completed the women's 5,000m final in 13th place.The race was won by Australia's Rose Davies, who completed a distance double after adding the 5,000m title to the 10,000m gold she had won earlier in the Games. Fellow Australian Jessica Hull finished second, while Scotland's Megan Keith claimed the bronze medal.India endured a difficult day in cycling.In para-cycling, Lisha Das was unable to qualify for the women's C4-C5 4,000m individual pursuit final.On the velodrome, Ronaldo Singh Laitonjam, David Beckham Elkatohchoongo and Rojit Singh Yanglem combined to finish seventh in the men's team sprint.India experienced mixed fortunes in bowls.The men's pairs team of Dinesh Kumar and Navneet Singh edged Botswana in a sectional play match after a tiebreak to strengthen their campaign.The duo will face Ian Barnes and Oliver Thompson of the Falkland Islands in their Round 4 Sectional Play match at 5:15 PM IST on Friday, July 31.In the women's singles competition, however, Nayanmoni Saikia was beaten by Malaysia's Emma Firyana Saroji.Although only two medals were added to the tally on Thursday, India finished the day with several encouraging storylines.Lovepreet Singh and Seema Kaliramna delivered podium finishes, Tejaswin Shankar remained in a strong position heading into the final day of the decathlon, all three Indian javelin throwers advanced, and both triple jump athletes secured places in the final.With multiple medal opportunities still to come, India closes Day 8 with 17 medals and plenty left to compete for during the final days of the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: David Liti's 223kg stunner denies Lovepreet Singh Commonwealth Games gold by one kilogram in weightlifting

India's weightlifting team ended its Commonwealth Games 2026 campaign with another medal on Thursday after Lovepreet Singh won silver in the men's 110+kg category in Glasgow.It was India's eighth medal in weightlifting at the Games. Earlier, Mirabai Chanu (women's 48kg - gold), Rishikanta Singh (men's 60kg - silver), Muthupandi Raja (men's 65kg - silver), Bindyarani Devi (women's 58kg - bronze), Gyaneshwari Yadav (women's 53kg - silver), Valluri Ajaya Babu (men's 79kg - silver), and Harjinder Kaur (women's 69kg - silver) had also finished on the podium.Weightlifting has two disciplines — the snatch and the clean and jerk. Each lifter gets three attempts in both events. In the snatch, the barbell is lifted from the ground to overhead in one movement with a wide grip. In the clean and jerk, the lifter first brings the barbell to the shoulders (clean), pauses, and then lifts it overhead (jerk), holding it steady until the buzzer.Lovepreet made a strong start by lifting a Commonwealth Games record 176kg in the snatch to finish first in that section. He held a 10kg lead over New Zealand's David Andrew Liti, who lifted 166kg, while England's Andrew Griffiths was third with 165kg.The 28-year-old from Amritsar then lifted 212kg in the clean and jerk to finish with a total of 388kg.However, Liti produced a Commonwealth Games record lift of 223kg in the clean and jerk to move ahead of the Indian and win gold with a total of 389kg, just one kilogram more than Lovepreet. Liti had lifted 166kg in the snatch.Griffiths won the bronze medal with a total lift of 356kg, made up of 165kg in the snatch and 191kg in the clean and jerk.Lovepreet led the competition through his first five lifts, but Liti's final lift changed the result. The New Zealander made up a 15kg gap with his last clean and jerk attempt to take the gold medal.Despite missing gold by just one kilogram, Lovepreet improved on the bronze medal he won at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham.His silver medal also ensured India finished the weightlifting competition with eight medals.

Article Title: ‘I’m a black African’: Commonwealth Games boxer Aziz Abdul’s racism claim rejected after headbutt disqualification
Article Text:
Aziz Abdul’s racism claim rejected after Commonwealth Games headbutt disqualification against England’s Damar Thomas/ Image: Screengrab

Disqualification ends Abdul's medal bid

Abdul alleges unfair treatment

Commonwealth Sport dismisses allegations

Thomas turns attention to semi-final

Abdul's family background drew attention before the Games

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Commonwealth Sport has rejected allegations of racism made by Ugandan boxer Aziz Abdul following his disqualification at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, with organisers insisting the decision against him was a legitimate field-of-play ruling made under the competition's officiating procedures.Abdul, who was disqualified during his super-heavyweight quarter-final against England's Damar Thomas, claimed officials had treated him unfairly because he was "a black African". His comments were later dismissed by Commonwealth Sport president Donald Rukare, who said athletes were treated fairly and without discrimination.The controversy followed a bout that ultimately guaranteed Thomas at least a bronze medal while ending Abdul's hopes of securing Uganda's first Commonwealth boxing medal since 1990.The quarter-final became increasingly physical as it progressed.Abdul was first given a standing count during the opening round, resulting in a point deduction.He was then penalised again for repeatedly punching after the referee had called a break between the fighters.The contest came to an abrupt conclusion early in the third round when referee Manuel Vilarino of Argentina ruled that Abdul had headbutted Thomas while the pair were grappling.The decision resulted in Abdul's immediate disqualification, sending Thomas through to the semi-finals and guaranteeing the England boxer at least a bronze medal.At the time of the stoppage, Abdul was trailing on all of the judges' scorecards.Speaking afterwards, Abdul disputed both the referee's decision and the way the contest had been officiated."Of course it's unfair," he said."When you watch the previous fights of England, their boxers play a lot of bullshit. They cannot judge them wrong."I took a light punch and they counted. I landed a heavy punch on him and they deducted my points and warned me."Abdul then alleged that his nationality and background had influenced the officiating."I'm a black African, I know," he said."It's God's plan. I don't know why the officials are scared about this fight. Why can't they let this fight continue?"He also insisted that the decisive incident was accidental."He elbowed me. He caught me with the elbow. It [the head movement] was not intentional. I was trying to come back. How can I headbutt someone? I would not.""He was the person they wanted to win. He was the winner before. I knew if I did not get knockout I could not win the fight." BBC Sport also reported that, while answering questions after the contest, Abdul referred to Thomas using a racial slur.Commonwealth Sport president Donald Rukare rejected Abdul's allegations, saying organisers had confidence in the integrity of the competition.Rukare, who is also from Uganda, told BBC Sport:"We at Commonwealth Sport believe every athlete is treated fairly and in a non-discriminatory manner."We are inclusive. That was a field-of-play decision and something that was said in the heat of the moment."He added that organisers believed the competition had been conducted fairly."As far as we're concerned, we have a good relationship with World Boxing, the athletes are treated fairly, so as far as we're concerned it was a fair playing field."Rukare also indicated that Abdul's comments could be examined internally by the Ugandan delegation."We have a team manager and chef de mission and I am sure the appropriate channels will be followed."We have a code of conduct. I don't represent Uganda here. I am sure that matter will be handled appropriately with our own code of conduct."Thomas admitted that advancing through a disqualification was not how he had hoped to reach the last four."It's not the way I wanted to win," the England boxer said."I can't change what happened today but I can control how I box on Friday."Before the tournament, Abdul attracted attention because he is the grandson of former Ugandan president Idi Amin.Ahead of the super-heavyweight competition, Abdul told BBC Sport that he wanted to become the new "King of Scotland", referencing a title Idi Amin bestowed upon himself in 1976.Idi Amin ruled Uganda after seizing power in a military coup in 1971. His government has been widely documented by historians as being responsible for widespread human rights abuses, with estimates suggesting hundreds of thousands of people were killed during his rule. He was also known by the nickname "the Butcher of Uganda."Abdul has previously said he never met his grandfather. In an earlier interview, he also stated that he was "inspired" by Amin, although it was not made clear whether he was referring specifically to his grandfather's boxing background or to other aspects of his life.Idi Amin himself had been a boxer before entering politics and developed a long-standing fascination with Scotland after serving with the King's African Rifles. He was known for wearing kilts, playing the bagpipes and proclaiming himself "King of Scotland", a title that later inspired the Oscar-winning film The Last King of Scotland.The boxer entered Glasgow 2026 aiming to secure Uganda's first Commonwealth Games boxing medal since the Auckland Games in 1990, but his campaign instead ended in controversy following his disqualification and the subsequent rejection of his allegations by Commonwealth Sport.
Article Summary: Aziz Abdul was disqualified during his super-heavyweight quarter-final against England's Damar Thomas. Abdul claimed officials had treated him unfairly because he was "a black African" His comments were later dismissed by Commonwealth Sport president Donald Rukare, who said athletes were treated fairly and without discrimination.

Article Title: ‘Absolute unity’: Insider exposes UEFA’s furious response inside emergency FIFA boycott meeting
Article Text:

UEFA approves unified boycott position

Insider describes unanimous opposition

Opposition continues to build across European football

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Politico

European football's opposition to FIFA's proposed commercial restructuring intensified on Thursday after UEFA's 55 member associations unanimously backed a boycott of FIFA competitions, including the men's and women's World Cups, should the governing body proceed with plans to sell a stake in the commercial rights to its tournaments.The decision followed an emergency meeting chaired by UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin, with European football presenting its strongest collective response yet to FIFA president Gianni Infantino's proposal to establish a new commercial entity that would oversee the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. An insider present at the talks revealed there was "absolute unity" across all 55 member associations in rejecting the plan.The meeting comes just days after FIFA formally asked its 211 member associations to vote on the proposal before a September 19 deadline.The dispute centres on FIFA's plan to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a new commercial subsidiary that would own and manage the commercial rights to FIFA competitions, including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing, licensing and related businesses.Under the proposal, FIFA would retain majority ownership while selling up to a 20% minority, non-controlling stake in the company to external investors, valuing the business at approximately $20 billion.The governing body expects the sale to raise around $4.2 billion.To secure support, FIFA has promised each of its 211 member associations funding of up to $40 million if the proposal receives majority approval before the September 19 deadline.The package includes an initial $20 million payment available from January 1, 2027, followed by a further $20 million through FIFA's development programmes.Infantino has defended the proposal, describing it as part of the "democratisation of football worldwide" and arguing that it would generate greater financial support for football associations while allowing FIFA to retain control over governance and sporting matters.Following Thursday's emergency meeting, UEFA announced that every one of its 55 national associations had endorsed a common position opposing the proposal.The governing body confirmed that its members would boycott FIFA competitions for as long as the investment plan remained in place unless FIFA completely abandoned the proposal. In a statement released after the meeting , UEFA said:"Europe's position is clear."We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation."As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership."Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination."There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments."Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale."Shortly afterwards, the Football Association issued its own statement confirming that it supported UEFA's position and opposed FIFA's proposal.An insider who was present at the meeting with all 55 UEFA member associations has revealed further details of the discussions, describing a rare moment of complete alignment across European football.Speaking to BBC Radio Wales , Professor Laura McAllister said there had been total unity in rejecting the proposal."There was absolute unity about the need to stop this catastrophic proposal of selling off part of football to private equity," she said.She argued that allowing private investment into FIFA's flagship competitions would fundamentally change how football is governed."This poses a genuine existential threat to the game because the minute you sell off part of the crown jewels of football, clearly private equity has very different objectives and motivations to those of us who are custodians of the game."McAllister also warned that the long-term consequences would extend beyond the immediate financial benefits being offered to member associations."UEFA and FIFA are not-for-profit organisations in that all of the money that is made through massive competitions like the World Cups goes straight back into football."Even if you sell off 20% of the game, then that's 20% you never get back. Once you've done it, you've done it, and it effectively undermines the whole ethical base of what we're about in football."Professor McAllister went on to say she "really hopes the boycotts don't happen.""I feel optimistic they won't, because the reality is the powerhouse of world football is Europe."Thursday's meeting represents the strongest escalation yet in the widening dispute between FIFA and European football.Earlier this week, UEFA accused FIFA of attempting to commercialise the game's most valuable competitions without meaningful consultation, while the Football Association criticised the lack of transparency surrounding the proposal.The European Football Clubs organisation, which represents more than 850 clubs, also condemned FIFA's handling of the plan, saying such a significant proposal should never have been introduced without proper consultation with the wider football community.The investment proposal has also prompted senior European football officials to begin discussing potential alternatives to Infantino's leadership ahead of the 2027 FIFA presidential election, withpreviously reporting that Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi has emerged in internal discussions as a possible challenger, although his representatives have said he has "absolutely no ambition, no intention, no interest" in seeking the role.With FIFA's member associations now facing a September 19 deadline to vote on the proposal, Thursday's emergency meeting has demonstrated that European football is prepared to oppose the plan collectively, raising the prospect of an unprecedented split between FIFA and its largest continental confederation should the proposal move forward.
Article Summary: UEFA's 55 member associations unanimously backed a boycott of FIFA competitions. Decision followed an emergency meeting chaired by UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin. European football presenting its strongest collective response yet to FIFA president Gianni Infantino's proposal to establish a new commercial entity. FIFA would retain majority ownership while selling a 20% minority stake to external investors.

Article Title: India to play Brazil in Kolkata friendly

Panaji: After Pele and Lionel Messi, Kolkata will roll out the red carpet for Brazil as the five-time world champions arrive in India later this year for a friendly against the national football team.The friendly at the Vivekananda Yuva Bharati Krirangan on Oct 3 is part of Brazil’s Asia Tour, their first in over two decades. As part of the tour, football’s most decorated nation will play two games against Australia on Sept 25 and Sept 29, before they arrive in India.India – now ranked a poor 138 -- have in the past played powerhouses like France (1948 Olympics), Yugoslavia (1952 Olympics) and Argentina (1984 Nehru Cup). For the first time, however, the country will be up against a side that is currently ranked among the top five in the world and often referred to as 'o País do Futebol' or the country of football. No wonder the organisers are keen to dub this as the biggest match in South Asian football history.“To welcome a team of Brazil's stature to our country is an extraordinary moment and one that will undoubtedly become a landmark chapter in the history of Indian football,” said All India Football Federation (AIFF) deputy secretary general M Satyanarayan.The Brazil football federation (CBF) has signed a letter of intent with the AIFF through Best11Group, an international sports consultancy firm.“It will be a special encounter with a country that has the largest international fanbase of the Brazilian national team who, for generations, has followed Brazilian football with immense affection and passion,” CBF said in a statement late on Thursday. “We are eager to live this moment alongside millions of Indian fans.”The organisers are expected to spend an estimated Rs 60-70 crore for a Brazil stop in India. The contract makes it mandatory for the former champions to field its A team, who will also feature against fellow World Cuppers Australia. This will pave the way for some of the world’s best-known footballers to play on Indian soil.“Our discussions were always centred around Brazil playing against India and no other opponent in the country. It’s a mismatch in rankings (5 vs 138), but India need to play such high-profile matches to raise its stature,” said the official.Brazil had a disappointing FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign where they were knocked out by Norway in the round of 16. Coach Carlo Ancelotti, who has turned down an offer from Italy to guide their national team, is eager to bounce back and is already working on a new era for Brazil, with the World Cup 2030 as the ultimate target.During the Sep 21-Oct 6 international match window, India are also committed to playing in the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup as one of the invitational teams outside the southeast Asian region but will have its strongest squad for the friendly against Brazil at home.Brazil’s arrival will continue a rich tradition in Kolkata, the Mecca of Indian football.The city hosted star-studded New York Cosmos, led by Pele, against local giants Mohun Bagan in 1977, while Argentina coach Alejandro Sabella broke the mould back in 2011 when he made Lionel Messi his captain, against Venezuela, in the City of Joy.

The organisers are expected to spend an estimated Rs 60-70 crore for a Brazil stop in India. Brazil had a disappointing FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign where they were knocked out by Norway in the round of 16.

Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi has emerged as the leading figure being discussed by senior European football officials as a potential challenger to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, according to multiple reports, as opposition continues to grow over FIFA's controversial proposal to sell stakes in the commercial rights to the World Cup.The discussions come as European football authorities intensify their resistance to Infantino's plan to establish a new commercial company that would oversee FIFA's competitions while allowing outside investors to acquire a 20% minority, non-controlling stake in the business.Although Al-Khelaifi has been identified as one of the most influential figures capable of mounting a challenge, his representatives have insisted he has no interest in seeking FIFA's highest office.According to Politico , conversations among senior European football officials about identifying a potential challenger to Infantino began during last month's FIFA World Cup and have accelerated following the backlash against FIFA's proposed commercial restructuring.Three senior international football officials, speaking anonymously to, said Al-Khelaifi has emerged as a serious candidate ahead of the next FIFA presidential election, scheduled for March 2027.Infantino has led FIFA since 2016, winning every presidential election unopposed, and announced during FIFA's Congress in Vancouver in April that he intends to seek another four-year term, which would extend his presidency until 2031.One European Union official closely monitoring FIFA's proposal told: "The stars have aligned."The official added: "Whether he steps up is another thing."Despite the growing speculation, Al-Khelaifi has publicly dismissed suggestions that he intends to challenge Infantino.A representative for the Qatari executive told"Nasser has absolutely no ambition, no intention, no interest in the FIFA role, and he will continue to discreetly support all the institutions of world and European football."Al-Khelaifi currently occupies several of the most influential positions in football administration.Alongside serving as president of Paris Saint-Germain, he chairs Qatar Sports Investments and beIN Media Group, leads the European Football Clubs organisation, sits on UEFA's Executive Committee and is also a member of the FIFA Council.His influence within European football increased significantly in 2021 when he helped stabilise the European Clubs Association after the attempted breakaway European Super League project threatened to fracture the continent's football structure.The renewed focus on FIFA's leadership follows the governing body's proposal to create FIFA Forward Enterprise, a new commercial subsidiary that would manage the commercial rights to FIFA competitions, including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing, licensing and related business operations.Under the proposal, FIFA would retain majority ownership while offering up to a 20% minority, non-controlling stake in the company to external investors, valuing the business at approximately $20 billion.The investment is expected to raise around $4.2 billion, with FIFA working alongside JPMorgan on the deal. The lead investor is expected to be Thrive Eternal, a fund launched by Thrive Capital founder Josh Kushner, whose brother Jared Kushner is the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump. Needless to say, the involvement of the Kushner family has only intensified scrutiny of FIFA president Gianni Infantino's close relationship with Trump, which has drawn increasing attention in recent months.To secure support from its 211 member associations, FIFA has coupled the proposal with a substantial increase in development funding.Associations would become eligible for up to $40 million each if the proposal receives majority approval before the September 19 voting deadline.Infantino has described the proposal as an effort to achieve the "democratisation of football worldwide", arguing that it would significantly increase financial support for national associations while allowing FIFA to retain control over governance and sporting decisions.The proposal has nevertheless triggered one of the strongest public disagreements between FIFA and European football authorities in recent years.UEFA has issued multiple statements criticising the plan, describing it as a step that "crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross" and warning that "the soul and governance of football are not assets to trade."The governing body has also convened an emergency meeting involving its 55 national associations to establish a unified response.Reports have suggested that potential options discussed include a future boycott of the FIFA World Cup should the proposal proceed in its current form.The Football Association has also expressed concern over what it described as the absence of consultation and transparency before the proposal was announced.The European Football Clubs (EFC), the organisation chaired by Al-Khelaifi, also issued a strongly worded statement criticising FIFA's handling of the proposal."European Football Clubs (EFC) notes with serious concern the sudden, unilateral media briefings and announcement by FIFA about a potential new corporate structure for the commercialisation of certain football competitions," the statement said. The organisation said it was inappropriate that clubs had learned of the proposal through media reports despite representing more than 850 clubs whose players participate in FIFA competitions."As an institution that represents over 850 football clubs – whose member clubs, their players and communities are fundamental participants in football worldwide, not least in FIFA's competitions including all the international club competitions – it would be wholly appropriate for EFC to be fully consulted on a proposal of such magnitude," the statement continued."EFC learned about this proposal in the same way as most global football stakeholders – without warning and through the media."The organisation urged FIFA to undertake broader consultation before moving forward."EFC always seeks to work collaboratively and supportively with all stakeholders – FIFA, UEFA and all confederations, national associations, leagues, player and fan associations."In that vein, we urge for calm and thorough consultation on all topics affecting the football ecosystem, together with more rigorous and transparent governance processes put in place to protect the game for the long term."Only in this way can we build the right institutional frameworks and relationships required to promote the true success, stability and sustainability of football."While Al-Khelaifi has publicly ruled himself out of the race, reporting suggests senior figures within European football have already begun discussing possible alternatives to Infantino as opposition to FIFA's proposed commercial restructuring continues to grow.With member associations due to vote on the World Cup investment proposal in September and the next FIFA presidential election scheduled for March 2027, the debate over the future governance of world football has become increasingly intertwined with questions about who should lead the sport's governing body in the years ahead.
Article Summary: Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi has emerged as a potential challenger to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, according to multiple reports. The discussions come as opposition continues to grow over FIFA's controversial proposal to sell stakes in the commercial rights to the World Cup. FIFA Forward Enterprise would oversee FIFA's competitions while allowing outside investors to acquire a 20% minority, non-controlling stake in the business.
